newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania court rejects Briton's appeal.
newsitem.headline: Albania court rejects Briton's appeal.

text.p: An Albanian appeals court on Wednesday upheld a two-year jail sentence on a 34-year-old Briton convicted of sexually abusing two young boys.

"We find Paul Thompson guilty of the charges of immoral acts with persons under the age of 14...and uphold the sentence from the first instance court of two years in jail," Judge Fatos Qato said, reading the appeal court decision.
Thompson, who had been held under house arrest, would now be transferred to a jail cell. He can appeal further to the Supreme Court, Albania's final appeals court.
A lawyer for Thompson, of Ashford, Kent, had called for leniency and asked the court to allow him to leave the country immediately.
"He asks for mercy because he has to undergo tests after he donated his kidney to his sister," lawyer Delo Isufi said.
Isufi said that medical documents from Hammersmith Hospital in London testified that Thompson had donated a kidney to his sister and he needed to have regular examinations every year.
Thompson, a divorced father of two, was arrested on August 25 after befriending two boys, aged 11 and 12, and luring them to his hotel room.
The age of consent for heterosexual and homosexual relations in Albania is 14.
